slides.headline: In a 93-year-old scientific society's history, only three Indians had ever been inducted as Fellows. In 2026, the third one was a woman.
Prof. Kuljeet Kaur Marhas was elected a 2026 Fellow of The Meteoritical Society
slides.body: She became the first Indian woman to receive the honour since the society's founding in 1933, and only the third Indian scientist overall, following Devendra Lal and J.N. Goswami.

slides.headline: She studies isotopes and pre-solar grains in extraterrestrial material brought back by Stardust, Hayabusa and Apollo.
slides.body: Based at the Physical Research Laboratory in Ahmedabad, her research examines Calcium-Aluminium-rich Inclusions - some of the oldest solid material in the solar system - to understand how planets formed.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs its scientists recognized at the frontier of planetary science, not just space launches.
slides.body: A 93-year-old international society inducting an Indian woman for the first time shows Indian fundamental research earning recognition on the same terms as the field's oldest institutions.
